evidence: Plaut. Trin. 3.3.67: diem sermōne terere segnitiēs merast (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 1.57.9: tempus in convīviō luxūque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With tempus, diem, aetātem as object; it often blames the time wasted.

phrases.latin: Ad aditum dēnique, ut tempus fallerent, per lūsum latitāvērunt et quaeritāvērunt
phrases.english: Finally, at the gate, to pass the time, they played hide and seek
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum
